replies.text:
Step 2 checks:
- Automated abuse of reachable entry point: design says "Any website can trigger the link" — flooding already covered by listed threats 5 and 6; no sign-in, sign-up, email/SMS form, or data-returning API is stated, so no further case. Covered.
- Staff/admin screens showing user-supplied content: design mentions only "the payment confirmation screen pre-filled" in the app — no such screen exists. Not applicable.
- Money moving with no record of who did it: design shows a payment flow with no origin recorded — already covered by listed threat 7.
- Cacheable personal/financial pages: design says nothing about documents, receipts, or browser/CDN caching. Not applicable.
- Attacker text flowing into logs, exports, emails, headers: design states only "myapp://pay?to= &amount=" params; no logging, export or email sink is stated, so the unconfirmed URL-leak item rests on how it is built. Not reportable.
- Unconfirmed items: cross-app forgery (#1) and origin-recording (#6) duplicate listed threats 1/4 and 7; replay (#2) and payee-name enumeration (#5) depend on unstated implementation (no idempotency statement, no statement that a payee name is displayed); overlay/tapjacking (#4) attacks the stated one-tap pre-filled confirmation screen reachable from any site and is a different attack path from the listed "no re-authentication" and "fake app" threats — not covered.

{
  "schema": "threatline.threatmodel.v1",
  "issueKey": "EVAL-02",
  "sketch": {
    "components": ["mobile app", "deep link handler myapp://pay", "payment confirmation screen", "payments backend"],
    "dataStores": [],
    "externalServices": [],
    "trustBoundaries": ["external website -> mobile app deep link", "mobile app -> payments backend"],
    "dataClasses": ["payment"],
    "exposure": "public",
    "llmFeatures": false
  },
  "threats": [
    {
      "stride": "Tampering",
      "title": "Overlay or tapjacking turns the pre-filled confirmation into an invisible approval tap",
      "scenario": "Because the deep link lands the victim directly on an already pre-filled payment confirmation screen, a malicious app on the device (or a site chaining the link with its own prompt) can draw an overlay positioned over the Confirm control. The victim taps what looks like a harmless button, game control or cookie prompt and instead approves the attacker-chosen payee and amount. Unlike a fake app impersonating the scheme, here the genuine screen performs the transfer, so the payment is fully authentic and hard to dispute.",
      "component": "payment confirmation screen reached via myapp://pay deep link",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "rating": { "attacker": "anyone", "effort": "medium", "reach": "one", "harm": "money" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "The app registers a deep link myapp://pay?to= &amount= that opens the payment confirmation screen pre-filled. Any website can trigger the link." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V1.14.6"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-1021"],
      "plainLanguage": "Another app can cover the Confirm button so the victim approves a payment to the attacker without realising what they tapped.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Protect the deep-link payment confirmation screen against overlays",
        "given": "the payment confirmation screen was opened from a myapp://pay deep link with a pre-filled payee and amount",
        "when": "another window or overlay is drawn on top of the screen, or the window is not the topmost focused window",
        "then": "the app must block or ignore the confirm action (e.g. filter obscured touches / hide sensitive content) and require the user to re-engage with a clean, unobscured screen before any payment is submitted"
      }
    }
  ]
}
